svg.title: Question class picks a default staple, not a different theory
svg.desc: known_goal: sized bag, default fast_pass, rails are a graduation. open_ended: unknown evidence size in this graph, default thorough. Out of corpus (why Rome fell on hotels) is wish, not thorough. Mixed traffic on one overlay is normal; do not mix gold books.
svg.text: Problem class · same three staples
Class is a scope default + optional turn label. Mixed “book me X” and “why is X popular” on one overlay is normal.
known_goal
ORDER is a sized bag on this overlay.
You can design how much data to process.
“beach in Mexico, fun in April, ≤ $300 a night”
search place → narrow vibe → hop season → project
Hard $ / dates: rail when wired — not find.where ranges
Not every known-goal is a named_query. Lookups are find/search→project.
A rail is how a hot fingerprint graduates.
default · fast_pass
else scout, then commit
Travel narrative = six HTTP looks. Efficient form = one planned pipeline.
Do not document those as the same thing.
Success: compact rows (later: binds for a PREPARED).
open_ended
ORDER is grounded synthesis from this graph.
Evidence size is unknown. Cap first recall.
In-graph: “Why is Tulum busy in April?”
Out of corpus: “Why did the Roman empire fall?”
on travel-sample.inventory → wish / clarify, not thorough
default · thorough
thin map · scout → thorough
fast_pass is usually wrong (empty / shallow).
A PREPARED whose binds are “the whole why” is usually wrong.
Open-ended on Zeus ≠ Wikipedia. It is an unbounded budget on this overlay.
Operator rules
Do not A/B hotel funnels against Rome-essays on one gold book.
Split stamps / rails / books when the mix is chronic — not because one user asked a why.
Tune Zeus/Koten per class default. Same overlay may still see both turns.
